title: Dalaman (DLM) vs Antalya (AYT) Airport for the Turquoise Coast
metaDescription: Compare Dalaman (DLM) vs Antalya (AYT) for Fethiye, Göcek, Kalkan and Kaş. Real transfer times, costs, winter flights and open-jaw routes.

body.text: Choosing between dalaman vs antalya airport is the single logistics decision that shapes your entire Turquoise Coast trip. Pick the wrong hub and you lose half a day on the D400 highway; pick the right one—or split them on an open-jaw ticket—and your coastal drive flows cleanly from day one.
Which airport is closer to Fethiye, Göcek, Kalkan and Kaş?

[Dalaman Airport (DLM)](https://dalamanairport.aero/) is closer to all four western Turquoise Coast hubs: 25 kilometres from Göcek, 46 to 55 kilometres from Fethiye, 125 kilometres from Kalkan, and 150 kilometres from Kaş. [Antalya Airport (AYT)](https://www.antalya-airport.aero/homepage) sits 200 to 215 kilometres east of Kaş, Kalkan, and Fethiye, adding 60 to 135 minutes of driving depending on your base.

The road geography explains why DLM wins for the western coast. From Dalaman, dual carriageway and the Göcek Tunnel carry you swiftly toward Fethiye and south onto the Lycian coast. Approaching Kaş or Kalkan from Antalya means either tackling the winding, slower coastal D400 past Kemer and Finike or cutting inland over the higher Elmalı–Korkuteli plateau—both take roughly three to three-and-a-half hours.
How do transfer times and costs compare?

Private vehicle transfers (up to 4–6 passengers in a Mercedes Vito) generally cost €45–€65 from DLM to Göcek or Fethiye, and €95–€130 to Kalkan or Kaş. From AYT, private transfers to Kaş or Kalkan typically run €125–€165 one way, while short hops to Antalya Kaleiçi or Belek cost €35–€55.
Watch out for two hidden costs when comparing flight prices:

items: Göcek Tunnel toll: Drivers passing between Dalaman and Fethiye pay a small tunnel toll (usually folded into pre-booked private transfers, billed separately on rental cars via HGS tags).

One-way rental car drop fees: Picking up a hire car at DLM and dropping it at AYT (or vice versa) usually adds a €60–€120 one-way fee, which is often still cheaper and faster than driving three hours back to your arrival airport plus burning an extra tank of fuel.

Public transit reality: From AYT, Antalya's AntRay tram reaches the city centre cheaply, but reaching Kaş or Kalkan by bus from either airport requires transferring to the regional bus terminal (otogar) first—adding 90 minutes to two hours.

body.text: Which airport has more year-round international flights?

[Antalya Airport (AYT)](https://www.antalya-airport.aero/passengers-visitors/flight-info/international-arrivals) has dramatically more year-round international flights, maintaining direct daily and multi-weekly links across Europe, the UK, and the Middle East even in January and February. [Muğla Dalaman Airport (DLM)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Havalimani/Dalaman/AnaSayfa.aspx) is heavily seasonal: packed with direct UK and European flights from April through October, but reliant on Istanbul (IST/SAW) or Ankara domestic connections in winter.

If you are travelling between November and March—for example, hiking the Lycian Way, visiting [Termessos and Sagalassos](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/termessos-sagalassos-guide), or booking winter golf via our [Belek luxury resorts guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/belek-luxury-resorts)—Antalya almost always wins on direct flight schedules and fares. Even if your destination is Kaş in winter, a direct flight into AYT plus a three-hour transfer often beats a two-leg connection through Istanbul into DLM.
Should you fly into one and out of the other?

Yes—for any 7- to 14-day Turquoise Coast road trip linking Antalya's Roman ruins with Kaş, Fethiye, or Dalyan, booking an open-jaw itinerary (fly into AYT, depart from DLM, or vice versa) is the smartest routing choice. It eliminates 200+ kilometres of pointless coastal backtracking on your final day.

A classic 10-day east-to-west flow lands at AYT for two nights in Antalya Kaleiçi (visiting [Aspendos, Perge, and Side](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/aspendos-perge-side)), drives west to Kaş or Kalkan for three nights, continues to Fethiye or Göcek for three nights, and finishes with two nights in [Dalyan](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dalyan-iztuzu-guide) just 30 minutes from DLM departure gates. Reversing the route works equally well if flight times favour landing at Dalaman.

faq.q: Is Dalaman or Antalya Airport better for Kaş?
faq.a: From April to October, Dalaman (DLM) is usually better because the drive to Kaş is 45 to 60 minutes shorter (roughly 2 hours 15 minutes vs 3 hours 15 minutes from AYT). From November to March, Antalya (AYT) often wins because of direct international flights.

faq.q: How early should you arrive at Dalaman and Antalya airports?
faq.a: Allow at least 2 hours before domestic flights and 3 hours before international departures—especially on Saturday and Sunday changeovers between June and September, when Antalya Terminal 2 and Dalaman International security queues build quickly.

faq.q: Are Havaş or Muttas airport buses available at Dalaman Airport?
faq.a: Yes. Havaş and Muttas shuttle buses run from Dalaman Airport to Fethiye bus station and Marmaris bus station timed around domestic arrivals, though they do not drop off directly at villas or hotels in Göcek, Kalkan, or Kaş.

faq.q: Can you take a taxi from Dalaman Airport to Kalkan or Kaş?
faq.a: Official airport taxis operate 24/7, but pre-booking a licensed private transfer with a fixed rate is almost always cheaper, uses a larger air-conditioned van, and guarantees flight-delay tracking.

faq.q: Does Antalya Airport have separate terminals for domestic and international flights?
faq.a: Yes. Antalya Airport operates a Domestic Terminal alongside International Terminals 1 and 2. If you are connecting from Istanbul to Antalya on a separate ticket, verify which terminal your airline uses before booking transfers.

faq.q: Which airport is better if you are starting a gulet cruise in Göcek or Marmaris?
faq.a: Dalaman Airport (DLM) is the clear choice: Göcek's marinas are only 25 minutes away, and Marmaris harbour is roughly 90 minutes away—saving at least two hours compared to landing in Antalya.
